articles.title: How I built a cloud-gaming service with crypto-based access (Couchless)
articles.excerpt: I've been working on Couchless, a cloud gaming service: instead of buying a console or a high-end PC, you stream big games from remote machines to any device with a browser. A few things I learned bui…
articles.body: I've been working on Couchless, a cloud gaming service: instead of buying a console or a high-end PC, you stream big games from remote machines to any device with a browser. A few things I learned building it: Latency is everything. Encoding location and keeping the input path short matters more than raw bitrate. Access is handled with a crypto membership, so it's a service, not a token. Browser-first delivery removes install friction. If you're curious, it's at https://couchless.fun . Feedback from gamers and devs welcome - what would you want from a cloud gaming service?
articles.author: Owens Mark

articles.body: On 25 November 2026 we ran a strictly passive, read-only scan across 500 unique public business, web-agency, WordPress, and SaaS domains in Europe and North America ( 482 responsive 2xx/3xx websites , all aggregated and anonymized). The gap between AI-search adoption and basic web security stood out immediately: 35.3% (170 / 482) already publish a valid /llms.txt file 58.5% (282 / 482) ship zero of the 5 core OWASP browser security headers 78.4% (378 / 482) do not enforce DMARC ( 30.9% missing completely, 47.5% stuck on passive p=none ) Only 2.5% (12 / 482) publish /.well-known/security.txt Only 2.3% (11 / 482) block any AI crawler in robots.txt Full report and methodology: 2026 Web Security Headers, DMARC and AI Crawler Benchmark . 1.

articles.title: Running Metal Gear Solid 2 HD and Other SHIELD Ports on Android with adb
articles.excerpt: Sideloading an NVIDIA SHIELD game port onto Android looks fragile until you count the moving parts. There are really only three: get adb talking to the device, install the APK, and drop the OBB archiv…
articles.body: Sideloading an NVIDIA SHIELD game port onto Android looks fragile until you count the moving parts. There are really only three: get adb talking to the device, install the APK, and drop the OBB archive into the one folder the engine actually reads. Skip that last step and you get a black screen on top of a perfectly clean install log. The whole run takes me about 25–30 minutes, needs no root, and the same recipe works for Metal Gear Solid 2 HD and the rest of the SHIELD port catalogue. Before you start: the short checklist PC with Android Platform Tools installed and adb on your PATH — confirm with adb version . Device : an NVIDIA SHIELD-class Android device (TV box or tablet).

articles.title: Before you trust a funnel number, check where it came from
articles.excerpt: I once printed this, to a seller, inside a read I was selling: 24 of 27 openers leave before the first choice. It came from 27 page views minus 3 deep reads. Two counters stapled together, dressed up…
articles.body: I once printed this, to a seller, inside a read I was selling: 24 of 27 openers leave before the first choice. It came from 27 page views minus 3 deep reads. Two counters stapled together, dressed up as a funnel. His answer was five words: right diagnosis, invented measurement. The diagnosis was worth money. The fake proof killed the sale of it. So I rebuilt the method around one rule, and it is the only rule I actually trust. Every figure names where it came from, or it does not go in Three labels, no fourth option: FROM THEIR PAGE. Quoted verbatim, from the page as a logged-out visitor on a phone sees it. FROM THEIR COUNTERS. The number the owner showed me, quoted as given. INFERENCE. Something I worked out. State the formula, and call it a guess.
articles.author: Nix Ilands

articles.title: Does font subsetting improve LCP (or only file size)?
articles.excerpt: Font subsetting almost always reduces transferred bytes. That is not the same claim as “Largest Contentful Paint will improve.” Teams burn a sprint trimming glyphs while the LCP element is still a pro…
articles.body: Font subsetting almost always reduces transferred bytes. That is not the same claim as “Largest Contentful Paint will improve.” Teams burn a sprint trimming glyphs while the LCP element is still a product image, a hero poster, or a background video frame: the file gets leaner, but the Core Web Vitals story does not move. The useful question is conditional. Does subsetting sit on the critical path to the actual LCP candidate on this URL? Watcher’s Font Subsetting for Web Performance post covers tools and workflow (Apogee Watcher). When the LCP element is imagery, pair that with Image optimisation strategies for better LCP scores . What follows is the decision cheat-sheet: when subsetting is an LCP lever, when it is only a file-size win, and how to verify in one lab pass.
articles.author: Apogee Watcher

articles.title: ChatGPT just stopped being a chatbot
articles.excerpt: The most important upgrade in AI isn’t necessarily a smarter model. It’s the moment the model stops talking to you and starts building the interface you need. OpenAI has taken that step with GPT-6 and…
articles.body: The most important upgrade in AI isn’t necessarily a smarter model. It’s the moment the model stops talking to you and starts building the interface you need. OpenAI has taken that step with GPT-6 and Intelligent UI, a feature that allows the model to compose answers using charts, buttons, forms, maps, diagrams, and working tools instead of defaulting to paragraphs. Paid users on Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise received GPT-6 Sol on October 7. Free and Go users followed one day later with GPT-6 Luna on October 8. That one-day gap is significant. OpenAI typically rolls out new models gradually, separating free previews from premium access by weeks or months. This time, both groups got the new model almost simultaneously. The message is clear: GPT-6 isn’t an experiment or a teaser.

Instant chat will be exempt from the shared allowance, but OpenAI hasn’t disclosed how large the new limits will be. ChatGPT has grown into much more than a chatbot , with OpenAI introducing tools like Work and Codex to help users tackle everything from building presentations to developing apps. articles.body: The Australian version of Grand Theft Auto 6 does differ from the international version in one small way; players down under are not able to use cocaine from their personal inventory to briefly overpower their stamina bar. NZ reportedly has the same version. In GTA 6, baggies of cocaine can be collected (or skimmed from full bricks) and show up as a consumable on the item wheel in the same section as cigarettes, cigars, and joints. Using one triggers a buff that puts stamina in an overpowered state, albeit only for about 30 seconds. This function was never included in the Australian-specific version of the game, as it would have prevented GTA 6 from being classified in the country until it was removed.

articles.title: SpaceX launches secretive spy satellites from California for US Space Force (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched its fifth classified mission for U.S. national security this month today (Nov. 24), from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.
articles.body: SpaceX launched another classified mission for the U.S. Space Force (USSF) today (Nov. 24), sending an unknown payload toward orbit from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Space Launch Complex-4E at TK11:08 a.m. ET (1508 GMT) , carrying the U.S. Space Force's USSF-266 mission. It was the fourth mission SpaceX has launched for the military branch this month. While details about the mission's payload weren't disclosed, it's the fifth space launch in support of U.S. national security in the last two weeks, and comes amid efforts by the Space Force to expand its communications and tracking capabilities.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 24, 1947: The US Navy launches the 1st Aerobee sounding rocket, but it didn't reach space
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere . After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets , the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched. Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space .
